fatal_errors: The proposed CoCrFeMnNi FCC alloy is not the target AlCoCrFeNi2.1 L12/B2 eutectic HEA.
The molten-salt exposure above 400 °C bears no agreement with the target immersed reciprocating tests in deionized water at 25–100 °C.
The comparator is changed from duplex stainless steel 2205 to 316H stainless steel.
The configurational-entropy mechanism does not reconstruct the target mechanism involving thermal-shock phase retention, passive-film repair, and temperature-dependent tribo-layer stability.
The cited molten-salt evidence directly reports greater mass loss for the HEA than for 316H due to Mn dissolution, contradicting the predicted superiority.
No cited evidence demonstrates simultaneous sliding and molten-salt corrosion for the proposed material.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion problem and proposes a testable alternative, but it does not reconstruct the target material, environment, comparator, temperature range, thermal-shock treatment, or L12/B2-mediated mechanism. Its experiment could discriminate the alternative claim, although the arbitrary 20% threshold and reliance on total mass loss would not cleanly separate corrosion, wear, and their synergy. Most importantly, E2 supplies only generic HEA background, while E1 concerns corrosion without sliding and contradicts the claimed advantage over 316H. Thus the central performance prediction lacks valid supporting evidence.
